title: 'Scared To Make a Mistake' - Former NFL QB Sounds Alarm on Drake Maye's 'Timid' Playstyle Issue - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Hanczar ,
1 days ago
Although the New England Patriots are coming off an impressive 20-3 victory, quarterback Drake Maye’s style of play still raises concerns among some in the NFL.
A finalist for NFL MVP in 2025, Maye’s progression in his first two professional seasons is impressive. Expectations seem to rise every year for the 24-year-old, especially after he led the Pats to their first Super Bowl appearance since the Tom Brady era a season ago. With such big shoes to fill, could the expectations be getting to Maye’s head?
Characteristics of Drake Maye’s Game Come Into Question Ahead of Week Three In what shapes up to be an exhilarating AFC matchup, the Pats head south to meet the Jacksonville Jaguars for a Sunday afternoon tilt. Both teams enter the contest with a 1-1 record: New England coming off a win over Pittsburgh, Jacksonville coming off a loss to Denver.
Despite Maye and the Patriots’ convincing win a week ago, questions remain about the young gunslinger.
Former NFL quarterback Dan Orlovsky spoke on ESPN’s “Get Up,” where he was not shy in voicing his doubts surrounding the University of North Carolina product.
“He’s scared to make a mistake,” said O rlovsky when asked about Maye . “He’s playing very cautious and timid, I think they’re calling the offense very cautious and timid.”
Orlovsky goes on to illustrate two plays from Sunday’s win over Pittsburgh, in which Maye’s body language comes across negatively.
“Look at the quarterback’s right foot when he gets to the top of his drop, this is a designed Y-leak,” Orlovsky describes. “Just pay attention to Drake at the top, when you look at him at the top of his drop, does he look like a guy that’s convicted of what he’s looking at? Hop, hop, hop, soft [describing Maye’s movements].”

Orlovsky continued, “The design of the play is to get the tight end we’re highlighting wide open, he’s wide open, the number one guy. But Drake Maye just checks the ball down because his feet are so ‘I don’t know what I’m necessarily seeing.'”
The ex-Detroit Lion continues his evaluation of Maye with another hesitant decision against Pittsburgh.
“Drake Maye at the top of his drop, look at his feet, the pocket’s clean, it’s a three-man rush,” said Orlovsky. “He’s already taking off running, but the design of the play gets the number one guy open. That’s the tight end crossing at the goal line.

“Right now there’s a young man that is very cautious and scared to be aggressive with the football and try to be a ‘fitting balls into open windows.’ He’s cautious, he’s scared, and he doesn’t wanna make mistakes. I think that’s hindering his ability to go play right now.”
While it may sound wild to speak of an MVP candidate from a season ago in such a manner, PFN metrics align fairly similarly with Orlovsky’s evaluation. Using PFN’s NFL QB Impact metrics, the former third-overall pick lands 25th among 33 statistically eligible quarterbacks throughout two weeks.
Strongly contributing to Maye’s disappointing grade are his four interceptions and 3.3 adjusted net yards per attempt, ranking 32nd and 31st, respectively.
Luckily for New England’s man at the helm, the Patriots’ defense has been lights out to open the season, allowing just 16 points in two games. However, if the Patriots hope to return dancing for the Lombardi, Maye and the Pats offense will have to adjust.
This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .
